Notably, FE-assisted stress correction shrinks the failure surface, while accounting for strain non-uniformity substantially increases the predicted failure probability.

title: Manufacturing-informed, artificial-neural-network-assisted optimisation of Type IV composite pressure vessels through progressive damage modelling
abstract: Optimising the stacking sequence of Type IV composite overwrapped pressure vessels (COPVs) is challenging due to dome geometric complexity, progressive damage behaviour, and high computational cost. This study proposes an efficient optimisation framework for compressed natural gas (CNG) COPVs by coupling experimentally validated finite element modelling with machine learning. A high-fidelity finite element model incorporating dome-specific variations in fibre angle and layer thickness and progressive damage evolution via a VUMAT subroutine was used to generate a training database. Validation against four experimental prototypes yielded relative errors of 1.3–11.7% in burst pressure and 0.8–7.2% in composite mass, with good agreement in failure modes and dome thickness distribution. An artificial neural network (ANN) trained using physically informed secondary variables achieved high predictive accuracy, with a minimum mean squared error of 1.84 × 10 -3 and Pearson correlation coefficients between 0.9505 and 0.9987 for mass, burst pressure, and stress ratio. The ANN surrogate was integrated into particle swarm optimisation and genetic algorithm frameworks, identifying an optimal stacking sequence that reduced composite mass by 18.3% while satisfying the minimum burst pressure requirement and increasing dome-failure safety by 32.6%. The proposed ANN-assisted optimisation reduced computational cost by 96.28%, enabling practical and scalable optimisation of filament-wound COPVs with progressive damage modelling. Highlights : • Artificial neural networks enable optimisation of pressure vessel stacking sequences • Dome angle and thickness variations are captured using progressive damage modelling • Mass, burst pressure and failure location are predicted with high accuracy • Particle swarm optimisation reduces composite mass by 18% while improving safety • Machine-learning-assisted optimisation reduces computational cost by over 96%

title: Tough bioinspired composites through bone - bamboo hybrid gradient designs: Simulation, deep learning, and 3D-printing
abstract: Natural composites exhibit outstanding mechanical properties, refined over millions of years of adaptation through gradient architectures and hierarchical organization. Inspired by these principles, we present a strategy for designing hybrid bone–bamboo-like gradient composites and establish an integrated simulation-AI-3D-printing framework for their evaluation and validation. Using lattice spring simulation, we examine graded structures with monotonic, partially and randomly shuffled volume fraction sequences. Our results show that placing a high soft-phase volume fraction (46.80%) at the notch improves strength by ∼5% and toughness by ∼25%, due to enhanced crack deflection and distributed energy dissipation. To accelerate mechanical performance prediction, we train a deep learning model on 200 samples, achieving R2 scores of ∼0.8 for strength and toughness. The model generalizes across 1620 additional designs, capturing layer sequencing effects using only volume fraction inputs. Selected top-performing designs were 3D printed using a multimaterial printer, validating the simulation predictions. This work offers a mechanics-informed design framework that tunes notch-adjacent compliance through gradient sequencing to create hybrid gradient composites. Integrating natural design principles with AI and additive manufacturing, this study provides a pathway for developing tough bioinspired materials with tunable fracture resistance.

title: A data-driven multiphysical masking model for morphology prediction and process optimization in longitudinal–torsional ultrasonic-assisted milling of CFRP
abstract: This study proposes a data-driven multiphysical masking approach for predicting the cross-sectional morphology in longitudinal-torsional ultrasonic-assisted milling (LTUAM) of carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP). The coupled vibration trajectory is first analyzed to elucidate the synergistic effects of “minimum-point” and “repeated cutting” mechanisms on the formation of residual heights. Subsequently, dynamic vibration and acoustic responses are employed to infer real-time cutting states and refine the morphology predictions. A multi-criterion damage model, integrating the improved Tsai-Wu, LaRC05, and Puck fracture criteria, is developed. Furthermore, a deep Gaussian process framework with sparse autoencoding of acoustic signals is introduced to achieve probabilistic and interpretable prediction of fiber fracture heights under uncertainty. A dual-path fusion strategy is then established, which incorporates tool-tip cutting forces and spindle acceleration within a Graph Convolutional Network-Physics-Informed Neural Network hybrid architecture to create a physics-constrained morphology model. By integrating physical masking with a multi-head self-attention mechanism, a multi-source fusion predictor is constructed. Experimental results demonstrate the framework's high predictive accuracy (95.24%) across varied machining conditions and identify an optimal parameter set (n = 1600 r/min, d = 8 mm, f = 5 mm/s, MQL; Sa = 2.1 μm). The proposed framework provides an innovative solution for CFRP ultrasonic-assisted precision machining that integrates physical interpretability, probabilistic prediction capability, and uncertainty-aware learning characteristics.

title: Multiscale design and mechanical performance optimization of a bio-inspired S-shaped mortise-and-tenon honeycomb via deep learning and probability-driven modeling
abstract: Mechanical metamaterials featuring high energy absorption and tunable Poisson's ratios are of significant value in engineering applications. To address the inherent trade-offs among stiffness, stability, and energy-absorbing capacity in conventional negative Poisson's ratio (NPR) honeycombs, this study proposes a bio-inspired s-shaped mortise-and-tenon honeycomb (BSMTH) inspired by the sutural interlocking features of beetle elytra. First, an s-shaped unit cell with asymmetric geometric features is constructed, and an analytical mechanical model is established based on the energy method. This model elucidates the effects of thickness (t), central angle (θ), and a thickness coefficient (k) associated with the joint distribution on the equivalent elastic constants, enabling the partial decoupling of the Poisson's ratio and structural stiffness. Second, 12 types of specimens (categorized into three groups) with diverse joint configurations were fabricated via fused deposition modeling (FDM). Tensile, compressive, and three-point bending tests were conducted across four polymer substrates to systematically analyze the effects of the material system and joint distribution on deformation evolution, failure modes, and energy absorption. The results indicate that the matrix material and configuration jointly affect the comprehensive performance of BSMTH. Within the investigated design space, a deep neural network (DNN) surrogate model was further developed and coupled with the integrated with non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) to achieve global optimization of the thickness gradient distribution, resulting in a 16.8% increase in SEA and a 13% increase in mean crushing force (MCF). This study provides a valuable reference for multiscale design and property modulation.

title: A progressive damage model-assisted GW-Gaussian process SHM method for complex composite damage quantification
abstract: Accurate damage quantification of composites by using structural health monitoring (SHM) is of great significance for the life management of aerospace structures. However, damage mechanism in composite structures is always complicated and progressive due to their heterogeneity and anisotropy, leading to significant dispersion and multi-stage characteristics in damage evolution. To solve this problem, a new progressive damage quantification SHM method for composite structures by combining Gaussian process (GP)-based probabilistic mode transition and progressive damage model assistance is proposed in this paper. The dominant progressive damage mechanism transition is identified by evaluating the statistical consistency between damage features and the GP predictive distribution. By combining the assistance of progressive damage modeling in capturing the entire damage evolution process, a mode-dependent GP probabilistic model is established to quantify the progressive damage. Based on active guided wave (GW)-SHM, the proposed method is validated under quasi-static shear loading using a composite orthogrid stiffened panel with a central cutout, which is derived from an important load-carrying component in reusable launch vehicles (RLV). The validation focuses on skin-stiffener debonding and subsequent skin cracking, which are the dominant progressive damage modes in such structures. Validation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately identifying the debonding-to-cracking transition at a load level of 200 kN, as well as in quantifying the debonding area with a maximum absolute error of 8.1%. A sensitivity analysis further confirms the robustness of the method under ±20% variations in key skin–stiffener interface properties.

title: 3D damage imaging and residual compressive strength prediction for arched composites: A CNT self-sensing approach with electromechanical modeling and machine learning
abstract: Fiber-reinforced polymer composites (FRPCs) are widely used in the automotive, aerospace, and energy sectors owing to their high specific stiffness and strength. However, their susceptibility to impact-induced damage motivates the development of structural health monitoring (SHM) techniques that can complement traditional non-destructive evaluation. This study presents an integrated SHM framework for non-planar arched composite structures by combining an optimized carbon nanotube sensing layer, three-dimensional electrical impedance tomography, electromechanical modeling, and ensemble machine learning. An electromechanically coupled model calibrated from experimental data was used to simulate damage evolution and piezoresistive responses. The three-dimensional generalized vector sample pattern matching (3D-GVSPM) EIT algorithm localized the dominant conductivity-reduction regions, with the normalized localization error from experimental values of 5.5%, 8.2%, and 12.7% for the 5 J, 10 J, and 15 J impact cases, respectively. A gradient-boosting regressor trained on simulation-generated data predicted residual compressive strength (RCS) with an R2 of 0.9817 on an independent experimental test set. SHAP-based interpretability analysis provided supporting evidence that the selected electrical features were physically consistent with damage-sensitive conductive paths. Overall, this study establishes a laboratory-scale diagnostic-prognostic SHM workflow that integrates damage localization and electrical-feature-based RCS prediction for arched composite structures under compression-after-impact conditions.

title: An open-source multi-sensor eddy current database for non-destructive characterisation of carbon fibre structures and analysis framework for eddy current inspection of CFRP composites
abstract: Open, standardised non-destructive testing (NDT) datasets for carbon fibrereinforced polymers (CFRP) are scarce, which hinders reproducibility,algorithm benchmarking, and data-driven defect characterisation in thecomposites community. This paper introduces EddyCus-HDF5, a publiclyavailable database comprising 738 eddy current scan files acquired with eightsensors (three absolute, five half-transmission) manufactured by Fraunhofer IKTS,covering five or more CFRP material systems and eight defect categories ateigen frequencies between 4\,MHz and 24.3\,MHz. The accompanyingopen-source Python software pipeline converts proprietary EddyCusASCII exports into a structured HDF5 format with full specimen, sensor, andinstrument metadata, and simultaneously indexes all scans into a queryableSQLite database. Two integrated signal-processing methods are presented:(i)~phase rotation for contrast optimisation, which scans the complex rotationangle $\theta \in [0^\circ, 180^\circ]$ and selects the angle maximising auser-defined standard-deviation contrast metric; and (ii)~Fourier-based fibreorientation detection (FOD), which extracts dominant yarn angles from the2D spatial frequency spectrum of each scan using a polar power analysis withbilinear interpolation. The dataset,converter software (MIT licence, v1.1.0), and example analysis notebooks areopenly available at https://github.com/itm-tud/eddycus-hdf5-converterand is archived on Zenodo with a persistent DOI. This resource providesthe NDT and composites research community with a reproducible foundation formachine learning and model benchmarking, sensor comparison, and algorithm development.

title: Multi-view deep learning for CT-based damage quantification in 3D woven composites
abstract: Accurate identification and quantification of damage in 3D woven composites (3DWC) are essential for understanding damage evolution and predicting mechanical performance. However, the morphological characteristics of cracks vary significantly across different viewing directions, leading to weaker identification accuracy when relying on a single view. To address this, we propose a multi-view deep learning approach that identifies cracks from three mutually orthogonal planes, thereby improving segmentation accuracy. In addition, a data-driven predictive analysis based on quantitative crack features is conducted to estimate shear stiffness degradation. To apply and evaluate the proposed method in practice, we conducted a stepwise experimental program as described below. Initially, a stepwise out-of-plane shear test was performed to enable progressive CT data acquisition during deformation. Subsequently, the proposed approach was adopted to automatically identify cracks from CT data. Based on damage visualization and quantitative analysis, interfacial cracking was identified as the dominant damage mechanism, and the shear failure process was classified into three distinct stages. Finally, CT-derived crack descriptors were used to predict shear stiffness degradation. Comparative evaluation with different regression models showed that the CT-derived crack descriptors contain useful predictive information for stiffness degradation, and that Gradient Boosting provided the best predictive performance under the present limited-data condition.

title: Point cloud-based deep learning for tensile strength estimation of gap-defective composite laminates using FEA-generated data
abstract: Gap defects in composite laminates can interrupt fiber continuity and cause localized stress concentrations, leading to degradation of tensile performance. Conventional finite element analysis (FEA) provides an effective means of evaluating such defect-induced strength reduction, but its high computational cost limits its applicability to large-scale defect assessment. This study develops a point cloud-based deep learning surrogate modeling framework for tensile strength estimation of gap-defective composite laminates using FEA-generated data. A numerical reference dataset containing randomly distributed and irregular gap morphologies was constructed through parametric modeling and progressive damage FEA, with controlled tensile tests on representative gap configurations used to support the finite element modeling strategy. To directly characterize complex layer-wise defect morphology, the generated gap geometries were represented as point clouds, and a layer-index feature was introduced to distinguish spatially overlapping points from different plies. A PointNet-based regression model, referred to as PC2S-Net, was adapted to learn the mapping between layer-resolved point cloud representations and tensile strength. The proposed surrogate achieved an R2 of 0.9489 and a mean absolute percentage error below 1.2% when evaluated against FEA-generated labels. Compared with modern point cloud architectures, PC2S-Net showed competitive predictive accuracy while requiring lower computational cost under the adopted preprocessing and training protocol. These results demonstrate that point cloud-based surrogate modeling provides an efficient and physically meaningful approach for numerical strength assessment of gap-defective composite laminates.

title: Data-driven acoustic emission framework with multimodal validation for resolving micromechanical damage in B4C/AA6061 composite
abstract: A data-driven acoustic emission (AE) framework with multimodal validation is proposed to resolve micromechanical damage evolution in a particle-reinforced metal matrix composite, B4C/AA6061, under uniaxial tension. AE waveforms are represented using wavelet packet transform–based spectral features and analyzed through a hierarchical unsupervised workflow. A key feature of the framework is the establishment of a matrix-referenced baseline using pre-fracture AE data from monolithic AA6061, enabling objective separation of matrix-dominant and particle-dominant acoustic activity based on autoencoder reconstruction error. The particle-dominant subset is further partitioned into statistically distinct clusters with characteristic spectral signatures and strain-stage dependence. To provide physical interpretation and validation, complementary in situ techniques are employed. In situ scanning electron microscopy (SEM) reveals the initiation and progression of reinforcement-associated damage, including interfacial decohesion and particle cracking. In situ neutron diffraction (NED) quantifies phase-specific lattice-strain evolution and captures the development of deformation partitioning between the Al matrix and B4C reinforcement. A clear correspondence is identified between the accelerated accumulation of particle-dominant AE activity and the increase in lattice-strain divergence during post-yield deformation, indicating progressive degradation of deformation compatibility. The integrated AE–SEM–NED analysis demonstrates that the proposed framework enables time-resolved and phase-sensitive interpretation of micromechanical damage evolution without relying on predefined signal labels. The approach provides a physically grounded basis for tracking reinforcement-associated damage and its coupling to phase-level deformation behavior in particle-reinforced metal matrix composites.

title: Deep reinforcement learning-based trajectory optimization for pressure vessel filament winding and analysis of multi-payout-eye co-layer hybrid winding
abstract: Filament winding trajectories govern component manufacturability and dictate mechanical properties via fiber distribution modulation. This study aims to develop more flexible and versatile trajectories by establishing a co-layer hybrid winding theory for multiple payout eyes and proposing a physics-guided deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based optimization method. A physics-based custom filament winding simulation environment was built to evaluate various algorithms. Additionally, a comparative dome training-difficulty score was introduced to assess morphology effects under the tested geometry and parameters. Finally, filament winding trajectory experiments under different objectives were conducted using a custom-built multi-payout-eye filament winding machine, thereby verifying the feasibility of the reinforcement learning-based trajectory design. The results indicate that, compared to Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithms, the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm exhibits the highest stability while maintaining high precision in the winding environment. DRL-based winding trajectories can achieve flexible and stable winding across different modes by employing a variable slippage coefficient. Within the tested geometry and parameter range, the score decreased with increasing aspect ratio, permitting greater offsets and design flexibility. Simultaneously, the winding of two distinct trajectories on the same helical layer is realized through the coordinated motion of dual payout eyes. This hybrid trajectory winding effectively mitigates fiber accumulation at the polar opening of the dome. Compared with the tangential path, the mean winding thicknesses of the adjacent and interlacing paths within the inner evaluation band were reduced by 43.9% and 50.6%, respectively.

title: An integrated process–failure simulation framework for predicting composite allowables via multi-fidelity stochastic simulation and machine learning
abstract: For material screening, qualification, and certification of aerospace composites, it is essential to establish statistical design properties that account for both inherent material variability and process-induced uncertainty. Regulatory standards require the determination of A-basis and B-basis statistical values as conservative lower bound design allowables. At present, allowables are determined through extensive experimental campaigns, which are costly and time-consuming, thereby limiting the exploration of new material systems. In this work, we present a multiscale, multi-fidelity process-failure modeling framework that enables the simulation-informed estimation of allowables. The framework integrates thermo-chemical-mechanical process simulations with stochastic multi-fidelity failure simulations to capture the effects of curing-induced properties, residual stresses, and microstructural variability on mechanical performance. A transfer-learning-enabled surrogate model accelerate uncertainty propagation across scales, while Bayesian inference leverages limited experimental data to quantify uncertain parameters. High-fidelity macroscale failure simulations then predict tensile strength distributions from which A- and B-basis allowables are estimated. Application to Hexcel AS4/8552 cross-ply laminates demonstrates close agreement with test data, with conservative predictions of statistical allowables. By linking manufacturing process simulation, process-induced residual stresses, stochastic failure analysis, Bayesian calibration, and allowable estimation, the framework provides a pathway toward simulation-informed composite qualification with the potential to reduce experimental effort.

title: Predicting inclusion-type internal defects in composites with complex structural shapes from experimental infrared thermography and numerical simulations: A demonstration of a machine learning approach based on graph neural networks
abstract: This study proposes a machine learning-based framework for predicting three-dimensional internal defects in a complex-shaped carbon fiber reinforced plastic (CFRP) specimen, using experimentally measured thermoelastic and computational FEA stress distributions. The proposed method employs a graph neural network (GNN), which directly incorporates the FEA mesh. First, high-frequency noise in the thermoelastic two-dimensional stress distribution is removed via Fourier analysis. Then the denoised field is mapped, using partial least squares and Gaussian process regression, into the principal component analysis (PCA) latent space of two-dimensional FEA stress distributions. Next, a multi-layer perceptron projects the latent variables of the two-dimensional stress fields into the latent space of the three-dimensional FEA stress distributions. The resulting latent variables are then reconstructed via PCA to obtain the three-dimensional stress distribution. Finally, the reconstructed three-dimensional stress distribution is input to a GNN trained on FEA datasets to predict three-dimensional internal defects. Conventional nondestructive inspection techniques for CFRP structures, such as X-ray imaging and ultrasonic testing, face safety, cost, and geometric constraints. In contrast, infrared stress measurement offers safer, simpler, and real-time inspection within the field of view. The proposed method estimates internal defect positions from surface stress information and provides a basis for reducing expert-dependent interpretation in future workflows. The present study demonstrates the feasibility of the proposed framework using one complex-shaped CFRP specimen with curved surfaces, such as a prosthetic-leg geometry, under the prescribed defect conditions.

title: Smart manufacturing in wire arc additive manufacturing: A comprehensive review of FEM-based simulation, machine learning, and digital twin technologies
abstract: Wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM) involves complex thermal microstructural mechanical interactions that govern melt pool evolution, heat accumulation, phase transformations, residual stress development, distortion, and final component performance. Accurate prediction of these coupled phenomena remains challenging due to the multi-scale nature of heat transfer, material behavior, and process dynamics. This review critically examines recent advances in smart manufacturing approaches for WAAM, focusing on finite element method (FEM)-based modeling, machine learning (ML), and digital twin technologies. Particular attention is given to heat source modeling, thermal history prediction, constitutive modeling for residual stress analysis, thermal microstructural mechanical coupling, and material data requirements for reliable simulations. Recent developments in accelerated FEM techniques, including adaptive meshing, reduced-order modeling, high-performance computing, and GPU-assisted simulations, are assessed for improving computational efficiency. The review further evaluates ML-driven surrogate models for thermal prediction, process parameter optimization, defect detection, and real-time monitoring, as well as digital twin frameworks that integrate sensor data with physics-based simulations for adaptive process control. Unlike previous reviews that examine these technologies separately, this work establishes a physics data-fused modeling paradigm that links FEM, ML, and digital twins within a unified intelligent manufacturing framework. Current challenges related to computational cost, data availability, model generalization, and real-time implementation are identified, and future directions involving hybrid FEM ML models, physics-informed learning, and autonomous WAAM systems are discussed.

title: Recent progress in machine learning strategies in designing, synthesizing and characterizing new age metal matrix composites
abstract: Metal Matrix Composites (MMCs) are advanced materials known for their high specific strength, stiffness, wear resistance, and thermal stability, making them vital for aerospace, automotive, defence, and energy sectors. However, traditional trial-and-error approaches for their design and development are inefficient, costly, and inadequate for exploring complex compositional and processing spaces. Recent advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) have enabled a shift toward data-driven and predictive frameworks in MMC development. This review highlights AI/ML applications across the MMCs lifecycle, including materials design, processing, and characterization. It discusses the use of supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning models to optimize matrix–reinforcement combinations, volume fractions, particle morphology, and interfacial properties. The integration of physics-informed and hybrid models for capturing complex strengthening mechanisms and interfacial phenomena is also examined. Further, the review explores ML-driven approaches for real-time process monitoring, defect prediction, microstructure control, and parameter optimization. In characterization, AI techniques are increasingly used for automated microstructure analysis, phase identification, damage detection, and property prediction. Emerging trends such as multimodal data fusion, explainable AI, uncertainty quantification, and the development of open-access materials databases are also discussed. The review concludes by identifying key challenges, including the need for high-quality datasets, standardized methodologies, and better integration of domain knowledge, to enable sustainable and accelerated development of next-generation MMCs.

title: Deep learning-assisted precise segmentation and meso-structure quantitative characterization of 3D7d-BFRP XCT images
abstract: Precise segmentation, reconstruction, and quantitative characterization of the meso-structure in 3D7d braided composites are critical for evaluating their mechanical performance under complex loading conditions and varying process parameters. However, the severe yarn adhesion and complex internal topology of cured 3D7d braided composites hinder the accurate segmentation of X-ray computed tomography (XCT) images, posing significant challenges to precise meso-structure characterization. To address this, using XCT digital images of 3D7d-BFRP composites as a case study, this paper proposes a Mask2Former-based 3D7d-BFRP XCT images automatic segmentation framework. The proposed framework enables high-precision segmentation of the meso-structure, achieving accuracies of 93% for the yarn phase and 95% for the pore phase. Subsequently, utilizing the proposed meso-structure model instantiation and reconstruction algorithm based on three-round global optimization, high-fidelity 3D reconstruction and precise quantitative characterization of 3D7d-BFRP samples are achieved. The analysis results indicate that the yarn Fiber Packing Density (FPD) of the 3D7d-BFRP sample is positively correlated with the degree of extrusion and negatively correlated with the cross-sectional area. Overall, the compactness distribution exhibits a characteristic pattern of higher FPD in the central region and looser structure toward the edges. Meanwhile, the pore distribution follows a clear bipolar distribution pattern. This study provides robust data support and key guidance for optimizing braiding and VARTM processes to reduce internal defects.

title: Physics-Informed Topological Graph Neural Networks for micromechanical insights and uncertainty quantification in void-containing composites
abstract: Predicting the performance uncertainty of porous composites necessitates capturing the highly non-linear damage mechanisms governed by authentic defect morphologies. This study proposes an integrated experimental-computational framework to unravel these complex micromechanisms. First, high-resolution in-situ micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) is utilized to extract stochastic, process-induced void topologies, directly informing the reconstruction of experimentally validated, elastoplastic Representative Volume Elements (RVEs). To decisively overcome the prohibitive computational cost of finite element analysis (FEA) for large-scale stochastic evaluation, we develop the Physics-Informed Topological Graph Attention Network (PIT-GAT). By abstracting microstructures into a primal–dual graph and integrating label-free physical soft constraints with weakest-link statistical pooling, PIT-GAT achieves an O(104) speedup over traditional non-linear solvers. Leveraging Explainable AI (XAI), the model autonomously reveals that void coalescence is fundamentally driven by diagonal plastic shear bands (30°–45°) rather than perpendicular Mode-I tearing. Furthermore, it naturally captures the classical size effect of void clusters. Finally, predictive uncertainty is reframed as a physically meaningful proxy for material instability, probabilistically mapping this variance to potential micro-damage bifurcation loci to establish robust, risk-aware design guidelines.

title: Topology-constrained U-Net for delamination mapping in ballistic-damaged thin GFRP
abstract: Delamination severely degrades the residual strength of glass-fibre-reinforced plastic (GFRP) laminates impacted by ballistic projectiles. This study introduces TopoPrior-UNet, a U-Net variant named for its novel loss function that embeds Topological Prior knowledge (specifically, a persistent-homology shape-prior loss to enforce the global topological structure of the damage, and a level-set active-contour loss to refine fuzzy boundaries) to segment multi-layer delamination images from a digital single lens reflex camera (DSLR). An initial set of 24 raw panel images was expanded to a 480-image set through three augmentation schemes, enabling learning under extreme data scarcity. Compared with a vanilla U-Net, TopoPrior-UNet improved mean Intersection-over-Union to 0.9832 (+9.9pp) and mean Dice to 0.9915 (+5.3pp), achieving the best scores across six metrics. These gains stem from jointly refining fuzzy boundaries and enforcing global ply topology, as corroborated by an ablation study. The trained model operates in quasi-real-time (i.e., inference in seconds per image) and requires only surface imagery, offering a cost-effective and rapid alternative to traditional NDT methods like X-ray or ultrasonic inspection, which often require minutes to hours for acquisition. Such rapid, non-destructive quantification of delamination extent lays the foundation for on-site residual-strength estimation and timely structural maintenance. • TopoPrior-UNet: level-set contour loss + persistent-homology shape-prior integration. • mIoU 0.9832, mDice 0.9915; +9.9 and +5.3 pts over U-Net on GFRP delamination. • Robust learning from 24 images expanded to 480 via augmentation. • Back-lit DSLR imagery enables near-real-time delamination mapping. • Shows the value of morphology-aware priors for materials engineering tasks.
